summary: This diff untracks PROGRESS.md (adds it to .gitignore with an explanatory comment, deletes the currently-committed copy) to stop the recurring merge conflicts caused by every task branch writing its own narrative into the same tracked file (cited PR12/PR23/PR24/PR27, consistent with this repo's actual git log). I independently verified the .gitignore comment's factual claims against the real scripts rather than trusting the self-report: scripts/veridian-task.py's parse_progress_md() reads PROGRESS.md straight off the workspace disk (not via git) and cmd_checkpoint persists completed/remaining steps into each task's own task.yaml checkpoint history, so resume-context does not depend on git tracking; worker-entrypoint.sh's automated commits use 'git add -A', which correctly respects .gitignore and will simply stop staging the file going forward; and cmd_create's PROGRESS.md reset step (previously needed because a fresh worktree off origin/master inherited the prior merged task's 'complete' content) becomes a no-op-but-harmless once the file is untracked, since it unconditionally rewrites a fresh stub regardless of whether an old copy exists. The change is additive/config-only, touches no .github/workflows/** paths (satisfying the hard rule), and introduces no security-relevant surface. It does trade away one thing worth a human noting at sign-off: previously a merged task's final PROGRESS.md narrative became visible in the PR diff on GitHub itself; going forward that narrative only exists in the task's local task.yaml on the server, not in the GitHub PR history, which is a real (if server-accessible) reduction in GitHub-side auditability. The diff is correctly pre-classified tier2 purely on the mechanical heavy-deletion threshold (41 deleted vs 9 added, >20 deleted and >2x added) rather than because of any actual risk in the change itself.
